name: CNE
description: Extract structured findings from free-text clinical notes with a local LLM.

notes.description: One clinical note (.txt, .pdf or .docx), or a folder of them for a cohort. Folders are searched recursively and the extension is matched case-insensitively, so notes filed per patient and a `NOTE.PDF` off a Windows share are both found.
notes.label: Clinical notes

notes_type.description: Which fine-tune is being run, "TMJ" or "Ortho". It selects the system prompt, the context window and, unless a model is named below, the model itself -- they are two different models.
notes_type.label: Note type

output_dir.description: Where the extractions are written. Nothing is written outside it, and it may not be the notes folder itself.

model.description: The quantised GGUF model, named from what this server hosts. Left empty, the bundle named after the note type is used, which is the one fine-tuned for it. A hosted bundle folder holding exactly one .gguf resolves to it; one holding several is refused rather than resolved by sort order.
model.label: Model

max_tokens.description: The longest answer the model may give per note. An answer cut off at this limit is reported as a failure and never written: truncated JSON parses as nothing, and upstream wrote the fragment as if it were the extraction.
max_tokens.label: Longest answer (tokens)

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. 0 makes the same note extract to the same answer twice, which is what lets a result be checked.
temperature.label: Temperature

context_tokens.description: The context window, in tokens. 0 means the note type's own default (TMJ 6144, Ortho 2048).
context_tokens.label: Context window (tokens, 0 = auto)

seed.description: The sampler's seed, so a run above temperature 0 is still reproducible.
seed.label: Seed

device.description: "cpu" or "cuda". "cuda" offloads every layer of the model to the card, which is measured at 8-13x faster per note; it needs the CUDA build of llama.cpp, which this tool pins. Where that build is not the one installed, the request is reported as ignored -- `gpu_offload` in the report is what actually happened -- rather than passing silently as it used to.
device.label: Device
